summary.headline: Satin Creditcare FY26 consolidated PAT rose 79% to INR330 crores; Q4 PAT up 125% QoQ, with FY27 standalone AUM growth guided at 15-20%.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 consolidated AUM of INR15,174 crores (up 19% YoY), revenue of INR3,161 crores (up 23%) and PPOP of INR928 crores (up 23%). Consolidated PAT was INR330 crores for FY26, and Q4 PAT rose 640% YoY and 125% QoQ, which management attributed to lower credit costs and growth, not one-offs. Standalone GNPA was 3.1% at March 2026 and credit cost fell to 3.8% for FY26 from 4.6% in FY25, with Q4 at 2.5% standalone and 2.2% consolidated. Management guided FY27 standalone AUM growth of 15-20% and credit cost of 3-3.5%, and raised its 2030 consolidated AUM target to INR32,000 crores from INR25,000 crores.

financial_highlights.change: NIM 13.23% in FY26 vs 12.42% in FY25

financial_highlights.value: FY26 3.8% standalone; 3.55% consolidated; Q4 2.5% standalone, 2.2% consolidated (INR79 crores)
financial_highlights.change: FY26 standalone -77 bps vs 4.6% in FY25

segments.name: Standalone microfinance (JLG)
segments.commentary: Standalone AUM INR12,853 crores (+14% YoY) with disbursements of INR11,202 crores; UP is 23% of portfolio with PAR 90 of 3%, Assam PAR 90 0.7%, Punjab 1.5%. Stage 3 coverage 73% (from 67% in Dec 2025); on-book provisions INR273 crores (2.9%) vs RBI requirement INR172 crores.

segments.name: Satin Housing Finance (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: AUM INR1,267 crores, 3-year CAGR 36%; GNPA about 3%, CRAR 53.8%; ICRA A- stable. Average yield about 15.5-16%.

segments.name: Satin Finserv (SFL, MSME subsidiary)
segments.commentary: AUM INR1,054 crores, up 92.5% YoY, 3-year CAGR 66%; 121 branches in 14 states; disbursed INR255 crores across 34 green loans. Lending is secured by receivables, equipment and property, per management.

segments.name: Satin Technologies (STL)
segments.commentary: Enterprise tech (HRMS, LMS, core banking, cybersecurity, agentic AI); first two clients within two months of incorporation; strategic stake in QTrino (post-quantum cryptography) acquired January 2026.

segments.name: Satin Growth Alternatives (SGAL)
segments.commentary: SEBI licence received for INR200 crore Category II AIF, a gender-lens impact fund for rural MSMEs; MOU with SBI for co-investment; progressing toward first close with soft commitments.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone AUM growth 15-20% YoY, implying about INR14,800-15,100 crores.
FY27 standalone credit cost target 3-3.5% vs 3.8% in FY26.
Consolidated AUM growth management estimate about 25-30% (average), so consolidated AUM roughly doubles toward the 2030 target.
2030 consolidated AUM target raised to INR32,000 crores from INR25,000 crores; non-MFI share target 30% (17% today).

NIM expected stable at about 12-13% consolidated (management also cited 13.5-14% over a longer period); no explicit ROA guidance, but management said ROA should improve on FY26's 2.6%, and that a >3% ROA is 'positive' rather than guided.
Cost of funds expected stable to lower; management says it could fall further as repo rates decline.
risks_watch: Q4 overall collection efficiency of just over 97% versus 99.9% X-bucket; monitor whether April holds and whether geopolitics or inflation (fuel prices) affects collections and demand.
Consolidated PAT is sensitive to forex and treasury gains: INR144 crores consolidated derecognition gain, of which INR92 crores is FX-related; management says this reverses over time.
Q4 PAT surge partly reflects lower credit cost; sustainability depends on the 3-3.5% FY27 credit cost target being met.
Yield regulation: incremental MFI yield about 25% and RBI commentary on interest rates; management says the pricing is justified but did not comment on future caps.
Subsidiary ramp-up (SGAL first close, STL client wins) is still early; the consolidated 25-30% growth and 30% non-MFI mix by 2030 depend on it.
Standalone net worth (INR3,129 crores) exceeds consolidated (INR2,868 crores) due to an old revaluation gain, which has limited analytical value.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on asset quality, profitability and diversification, with strong claims on Q4 performance. Management was evasive on specifics: declined to give ROA guidance, the April collection-efficiency number and the Q4 absolute consolidated PAT, and gave a vague answer on the RBI yield question.
key_quotes: Consolidated PAT grew 640% year -on-year and 125% quarter -on-quarter.
We are not growing blindly. We are growing into our infrastructure with the discipline that has defined Satin.
So there is no question where I think it could be singled out as in terms of tax and it's an interest rate play which is going to be there.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about Satin Finserv's customer profile, collateral and underwriting approach.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SFL serves graduated MFI customers and green-finance/micro-enterprise borrowers, underwrites on cash flows and internal scores with data analytics, and lends on secured terms (receivables, equipment, property). It did not give a percentage of the book secured by property; LTV is about 40-45%.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked for April X-bucket collection efficiency and whether geopolitical issues are causing stress.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said April is holding at a similar level to Q4 (99.9%) but did not give a figure, and said there is no stress from the geopolitical situation in any state. Q4 overall collection efficiency was a little over 97%.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked whether there was any one-off in Q4 PAT, including forex.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no one-off; Aditi Singh attributed the Q4 PAT rise to reduced credit cost and the growth strategy. Management did not separately quantify the Q4 absolute consolidated PAT.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked for FY27 ROA guidance and whether ROA above 3% is achievable.
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give explicit ROA guidance, saying it is a function of AUM growth and credit cost; it said it expects ROA to be better than FY26's 2.6% and that the direction is positive.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about the consolidated AUM path to the 2030 target and the growth pace.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 15-20% guidance applies to standalone MFI only; consolidated growth is expected to average about 25-30%, which supports the revised INR32,000 crore 2030 AUM target (from INR25,000 crores).

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about the INR144 crore net gain on derecognition of financial instruments and whether treasury income is sustainable.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the consolidated INR144 crore line includes a INR92 crore FX effect offset by a corresponding finance-cost item, while derecognition gains are DA income and fair-value gains are treasury income on mutual funds and forex contracts. Management said treasury income is incidental to liquidity, and that NIM is broadly stable at 13.5-14% over a longer period.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about the RBI yield-cap risk and whether the MFI yield of about 25% is sustainable.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the regulator's interest-rate focus should be read in the context of financial inclusion, doorstep delivery, elevated credit cost and cost of funds, and risk-based pricing. It did not say how it sees future caps and said there is no question of a one-off yield cut.

capex_capacity: 392 new branches added in FY26; field presence in over 1 lakh villages and 550-plus districts; 2,015 branches and 577 districts as of the call, 34 lakh customers, 18,265 employees.
Presence in over 64% of India's pin codes; technology and AI used across underwriting, portfolio monitoring and risk assessment.
Liquidity of INR2,092 crores and undrawn sanctions of INR2,235 crores; ALM positive across all buckets; FY26 borrowings raised INR10,826 crores; 75 active lenders.
SGAL: SEBI licence received for INR200 crore Category II AIF; progressing toward first close with strong soft commitments; MOU with SBI for co-investment.

STL: first two clients acquired within two months of incorporation; strategic stake in QTrino (IIT Patna incubated, post-quantum cryptography) acquired January 2026; representative offices in Toronto and Dubai.
Management said standalone AUM growth of 15-20% in FY27 rests on branch infrastructure and ALM, and said it is growing into existing infrastructure rather than growing blindly.
demand_pricing: Sector: CRIF High Mark data cited by management shows MFI originations up 25.8% QoQ to INR77,555 crores in Q3 FY26; average ticket size up 18% YoY; sector PAR 1-180 days at 4.7% in January 2026.

Standalone disbursements FY26 INR11,202 crores; Q4 disbursements up 43% (per closing remarks); sourcing-to-disbursement ratio 39%; NATCAT insurance covered INR5,800 crores of disbursement since September 2025.

Pricing: average incremental MFI yield about 25% (management confirmed analyst's 25-26% reading as broadly correct); housing finance average yield about 15.5-16%; SFL green loans priced close to MFI yield.
Diversification: non-MFI share 17% of consolidated AUM today, target 30% by 2030. SFL AUM INR1,054 crores (+92.5% YoY); SHFL AUM INR1,267 crores.

Collections: Q4 overall collection efficiency just over 97%; X-bucket collection efficiency 99.9% in Q4 and said to be holding in April without giving a figure; management said no geopolitical stress seen in any state.
Cost of funds: marginal cost of borrowing 10.82%, down 43 bps; management said cost of funds should stay stable or fall as repo rates decline.

adds.what: 392 new branches added in FY26 (2,015 branches as of the call; no specific forward branch count given)
SGAL INR200 crore Category II AIF (financial fund, not productive capacity; SEBI licence received, progressing to first close)

growth.why: FY27 standalone AUM growth guided at 15-20% (INR14,800-15,100 cr), backed by existing branch infrastructure, ALM and undrawn sanctions of INR2,235 cr, with consolidated AUM growth estimated at 25-30% and 2030 target raised to INR32,000 cr; no specific new capacity timeline given beyond FY26 branch additions.
